questions.question: Under the hood, what is a Git branch?

options.A: A completely duplicated copy of all project files in a hidden folder
options.B: A lightweight, movable 41-byte pointer to a specific commit

questions.explanation: In Git, a branch is simply a file containing the 40-character commit hash it currently points to.

questions.question: Which modern Git command creates a new branch and switches to it in a single step?
questions.explanation: `git switch -c <name>` (or older `git checkout -b <name>`) creates the branch and immediately moves HEAD to it.

questions.question: Which command lists all local branches in your repository?
questions.explanation: `git branch` lists all local branches, highlighting the currently active branch with an asterisk `*`.

questions.question: What does `HEAD` point to in standard Git operation?

options.B: The currently checked-out branch pointer or active commit

questions.explanation: `HEAD` is Git's pointer to the current active branch/commit. When you commit, the branch that HEAD points to moves forward.

questions.question: Which of the following is a recommended professional branch naming convention for a new login screen?
questions.explanation: Prefixes like `feature/`, `bugfix/`, `hotfix/`, and `chore/` make branch purposes immediately obvious to team members.

questions.question: How do you switch back to an existing branch named `main` using modern Git?
questions.explanation: `git switch <branch-name>` switches to an existing branch.

questions.question: What happens to your working directory files when you switch to another branch?

options.A: Nothing — files never change when switching branches
options.B: Git automatically updates, adds, or removes files in your folder to match that branch's latest commit
options.C: All uncommitted files are permanently deleted

questions.explanation: Git swaps out files in your working directory to accurately reflect the snapshot of the branch you switched to.

questions.question: What happens if you try to switch branches while having uncommitted changes that conflict with the destination branch?

options.A: Git deletes your changes without warning
options.B: Git aborts the switch and warns you to commit or stash your changes first
options.D: Git automatically pushes the changes to GitHub

questions.explanation: Git protects your uncommitted work. If a file modified in your working tree differs on the target branch, Git blocks the switch.

questions.question: Which command lists BOTH local branches and remote-tracking branches from GitHub?
questions.explanation: `git branch -a` (all) displays local branches as well as remote-tracking branches (prefixed with `remotes/origin/`).

questions.question: How do you push a newly created local branch named `feature/login` to GitHub?
questions.explanation: `git push -u origin <branch-name>` creates the branch on GitHub and sets up upstream tracking.
